unit.bookReference: Lesson 15 Dialogue I, symptom vocabulary, health inquiry, and duration integration.
unit.label: Symptoms & feeling sick
unit.title: Symptoms and Feeling Sick
unit.description: Ask about discomfort, describe symptoms, and say how long a condition has lasted.

goal.text: 我一直流鼻水，頭很痛，胃口很差。
goal.pinyin: Wǒ yìzhí liú bíshuǐ, tóu hěn tòng, wèikǒu hěn chā.
goal.meaning: I have a runny nose, my head hurts, and my appetite is poor.

steps.explanation: 醫生 yīshēng means “doctor.”

steps.prompt: Which question asks where someone feels unwell?
steps.explanation: 哪裡不舒服？ is the health-inquiry question taught here.

steps.prompt: What is the speaker asking about?
steps.explanation: The question asks about the location of discomfort.
一直 describes something continuing without interruption in this symptom report.
流 liú means “to flow.”
鼻水 bíshuǐ is nasal mucus; 流鼻水 describes having a runny nose.
The audio says the speaker continuously has a runny nose.

lessons.title: Head and Appetite
lessons.subtitle: Describe head pain and poor appetite.

steps.explanation: 頭 tóu means “head.”
痛 tòng describes pain.
胃口 wèikǒu means “appetite.”

steps.prompt: In 胃口很差, 差 is pronounced…
steps.explanation: In 胃口很差, 差 is chā and means “poor/bad.”

steps.prompt: Which sentence says the speaker's appetite is poor?
steps.explanation: 胃口很差 means “the appetite is poor.”

steps.prompt: In 什麼東西都不想吃, what does 什麼東西…都 express?
options: totality under negation: not wanting to eat anything
a question asking which food the person wants
steps.answer: totality under negation: not wanting to eat anything
steps.explanation: This retrieves the earlier question-word + 都 pattern; negative non-specific question-word pattern is not taught until Unit 46.
喉嚨 hóulóng means “throat.”
發炎 fāyán means “to be inflamed.”

steps.prompt: Which best matches 喉嚨有一點發炎？
options: The throat is a little inflamed.
The throat has been sore for four days.
steps.answer: The throat is a little inflamed.
steps.explanation: 有一點 gives a slight degree here.

steps.prompt: What body part do you hear?
steps.explanation: The audio describes the throat.

lessons.title: Sick and Feverish
lessons.subtitle: Report illness and a slight fever.

steps.explanation: 生病 shēngbìng means “to fall ill / be sick.”
發燒 fāshāo means “to have a fever.”
發燒 is the fever expression.

steps.audioText: 我生病了，還有一點發燒。
options: being sick and having a slight fever
having a good appetite and resting
going to a pharmacy and taking medicine
steps.answer: being sick and having a slight fever
steps.explanation: 生病 and 發燒 are both present.

lessons.title: How Long Has It Been?
lessons.subtitle: Integrate symptom duration with the opening doctor–patient exchange.

steps.prompt: Which question asks about how long a current condition has lasted?
steps.explanation: 多久 asks duration; the final 了 fits the current-condition context.

steps.prompt: Which answer fits 大概多久了？
steps.explanation: The answer gives the duration up to now.

steps.audioText: 大概多久了？已經四、五天了。
steps.explanation: The question and answer concern how long the condition has lasted.

steps.prompt: Which sequence best matches the doctor visit so far?
options: ask where it hurts → describe symptoms → ask duration → examine throat
compare rent → ask duration → buy medicine → discuss weather
ask about insurance → reject help → examine throat → compare actions
steps.answer: ask where it hurts → describe symptoms → ask duration → examine throat
steps.explanation: That is the communicative arc of the opening doctor visit.

lessons.title: Unit 45 Review
lessons.subtitle: Retrieve symptoms, handwriting, health inquiry, and duration.

steps.explanation: 流鼻水 is the runny-nose symptom.
頭很痛 + 胃口很差.
The audio names the throat.
醫生 means doctor.
一直 means continuously.
流 means flow.
鼻水 means runny nose.
頭 means head.
痛 means painful.
胃口 means appetite.

steps.prompt: In 胃口很差, which reading/meaning pair for 差 is correct?
steps.explanation: 胃口很差 uses chā.
喉嚨 means throat.
發炎 means be inflamed.
生病 means be sick.
發燒 means have a fever.

steps.prompt: Which question starts a health check by asking where the discomfort is?
steps.explanation: This retrieves the health-inquiry frame and symptom vocabulary.

steps.prompt: Which pair forms a natural duration exchange?
options: 大概多久了？／已經四、五天了。
哪裡不舒服？／大概多久了。
steps.answer: 大概多久了？／已經四、五天了。
steps.explanation: This integrates the duration question with its duration-to-now answer.

steps.prompt: Which sentence uses the earlier Unit-40 question-word + 都 totality pattern?
steps.explanation: 什麼東西 + 都 expresses the earlier totality pattern under negation.

newVocabulary.note: A person who treats patients. 醫生 yīshēng is “doctor”; use it as a title or a noun.
Put 一直 before the continuing action: 一直流鼻水 means “keep having a runny nose.”
A verb for liquid flowing. In 流鼻水, it describes a runny nose.
The mucus from the nose. Use 流鼻水 for the symptom “have a runny nose.”
The body part “head” here. 頭很痛 means “my/the head hurts.”
Use after the body part that hurts: 頭很痛. It describes pain, not the action of injuring someone.
Appetite, not the stomach itself. 胃口很差 means “have a poor appetite.”
Pronounced chā here: poor or bad in quality, as in 胃口很差.
The two characters form one word, “throat.” Learn hóulóng together.
To become inflamed. 喉嚨發炎 means “the throat is inflamed.”
To fall ill or be sick. 生 and 病 form a separable verb, revisited later in this lesson.
To have a fever. Learn the whole word; it is not translated as “send out burning.”

醫.note: Medical care; learn 醫 in 醫生 yīshēng, “doctor.” The upper section has two blocks, with 酉 underneath.
醫.memory: Think of a doctor’s equipment on a shelf: two upper blocks above the wide 酉 base. Write the upper left, upper right, then the base.

parts.label: 医
parts.name: upper-left block
parts.description: The seven-stroke upper-left block encloses 矢; its final enclosing stroke comes after the inner strokes.

parts.label: 殳
parts.name: upper-right block
parts.description: Write this compact four-stroke block beside 医, above the base.

parts.label: 酉
parts.name: bottom block
parts.description: The broad seven-stroke 酉 supports both upper blocks.

直.note: 直 means “straight.” In 一直 yìzhí, it contributes the idea of continuing without a break.
直.memory: Stack the top cross above the narrow middle, then finish with the long bottom stroke. Picture a straight, continuous route.

parts.label: 十
parts.name: top cross
parts.description: The first horizontal and vertical cross above the middle.

parts.label: 目
parts.name: middle box
parts.description: Keep the five-stroke middle narrow and its horizontal lines evenly spaced.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: bottom stroke
parts.description: The final horizontal extends underneath the middle.

流.note: 流 means “to flow.” In 流鼻水 liú bíshuǐ, nasal mucus is flowing: “have a runny nose.”
流.memory: The three water strokes on the left remind you of flowing liquid; the right side ends in three descending strokes.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water component
parts.description: The narrow three-stroke water component goes on the left.

parts.label: 㐬
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Write the upper strokes before the three descending strokes below.

鼻.note: 鼻 means “nose.” 鼻水 bíshuǐ is nasal mucus; 流鼻水 means “have a runny nose.”
鼻.memory: Remember three stacked levels: 自, then 田, then the small base. Keep the levels centered.

parts.label: 自
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: The six-stroke 自 shape occupies the top.

parts.label: 田
parts.name: middle component
parts.description: The five-stroke 田 sits directly below 自.

parts.label: 丌
parts.name: bottom component
parts.description: Finish with the horizontal and two descending strokes beneath 田.

痛.note: 痛 means “to hurt; painful.” A body part can come before it: 頭很痛 tóu hěn tòng means “the head hurts.”
痛.memory: Use the illness frame 疒 around 甬. The frame links this shape with pain and illness.

parts.label: 疒
parts.name: illness frame
parts.description: These five strokes form the top and left frame; the two left strokes belong to the frame.

parts.label: 甬
parts.name: inner component
parts.description: Write the seven-stroke inner component inside the open frame.

痛.partOrderLabel: outer frame first, then the inside

胃.note: 胃 means “stomach,” the organ. 胃口 wèikǒu means “appetite,” rather than a literal “stomach mouth.”
胃.memory: A compact 田 sits above the flesh component 月. Keep the two blocks stacked, not side by side.

parts.label: 田
parts.name: upper block
parts.description: The five strokes of 田 form the upper block.

parts.label: 月
parts.name: flesh component
parts.description: This 月-shaped lower component is associated with the body here.

喉.note: 喉 is the first syllable of 喉嚨 hóulóng, “throat.” Learn and say the two-character word together.
喉.memory: A small mouth 口 sits to the left of the taller 侯. Both characters in 喉嚨 have a mouth component.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth component
parts.description: Keep the three-stroke mouth small on the left.

parts.label: 侯
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The nine-stroke 侯 is the larger right-hand block; it also cues the sound hóu.

嚨.note: 嚨 is the second syllable of 喉嚨 hóulóng, “throat.” It normally appears here as part of the whole word.
嚨.memory: Remember mouth 口 beside the detailed 龍 shape. Leave most of the width for the right-hand component.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth component
parts.description: Write the small mouth on the left first.

parts.label: 龍
parts.name: dragon component
parts.description: The sixteen-stroke 龍 provides the sound cue lóng; keep its internal strokes distinct.

發.note: 發 has several meanings. Here it means developing a condition: 發炎 fāyán, “be inflamed,” and 發燒 fāshāo, “have a fever.”
發.memory: Think of a roof-like top over two lower blocks: the bent 弓 on the left and 殳 on the right.

parts.label: 癶
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: These five spreading strokes form the top of 發.

parts.label: 弓
parts.name: lower-left component
parts.description: The three bent strokes form the lower-left block.

parts.label: 殳
parts.name: lower-right component
parts.description: Finish the four-stroke block on the lower right.

炎.note: 炎 relates to inflammation here. Learn 發炎 fāyán as “to be inflamed,” as in 喉嚨發炎, “the throat is inflamed.”
炎.memory: Two 火 shapes are stacked: heat above heat. Use that image to remember inflammation.

parts.label: 火
parts.name: upper fire
parts.description: The first four strokes form the smaller upper 火.

parts.label: 火
parts.name: lower fire
parts.description: The second 火 sits below and spreads wider to support the top.

病.note: 病 means “illness; sick.” 生病 shēngbìng means “fall ill / be sick.”
病.memory: The illness frame 疒 surrounds 丙. Keep the frame open on the right and bottom.

parts.label: 疒
parts.name: illness frame
parts.description: Write the five-stroke top-and-left frame first.

parts.label: 丙
parts.name: inner component
parts.description: The five-stroke 丙 sits inside; it provides a sound cue for bìng.

病.partOrderLabel: outer frame first, then the inside

燒.meaning: burn; have a fever in 發燒
燒.note: 燒 means “to burn.” In 發燒 fāshāo, the whole word means “have a fever.”
燒.memory: Fire 火 stands on the left; the tall 堯 block stands on the right. The fire is your cue for burning and fever.

parts.label: 火
parts.name: fire component
parts.description: The four-stroke 火 narrows to fit the left side.

parts.label: 堯
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Keep the repeated 土 shapes above the final lower strokes.

u45-dialogue-1-5.text:
醫生：你哪裡不舒服？
病人：我一直流鼻水，頭很痛，胃口很差。什麼東西都不想吃。
醫生：大概多久了？
病人：已經四、五天了。
醫生：我看看你的喉嚨。喉嚨有一點發炎。
u45-dialogue-1-5.pinyin:
Yīshēng: Nǐ nǎlǐ bù shūfu?
Bìngrén: Wǒ yìzhí liú bíshuǐ, tóu hěn tòng, wèikǒu hěn chā. Shénme dōngxi dōu bù xiǎng chī.
Yīshēng: Dàgài duōjiǔ le?
Bìngrén: Yǐjīng sì, wǔ tiān le.
Yīshēng: Wǒ kànkan nǐ de hóulóng. Hóulóng yǒu yìdiǎn fāyán.
u45-dialogue-1-5.meaning: A doctor–patient exchange about symptoms, duration, and a throat check.
u45-dialogue-1-5.note: Direct address uses 你; proper-name glyphs are not required.
